verdicts.title: transferVesting resets grantor releaseRate ignoring amountClaimed, letting sellers over-claim from the pool

a.reden: Both describe transferVesting miscalculating releaseRate by ignoring already‑claimed amounts, enabling over‑claiming

b.reden: Both describe transferVesting recalculating releaseRate without accounting for already claimed tokens, letting the seller over-claim.

verdicts.title: Referral reward is computed and emitted but never paid to the referrer

a.reden: The candidate describes a missing referral payment bug, which is unrelated to the vesting-related findings H-01, H-02, and H-03.

b.reden: The candidate finding concerns referral reward not being paid, while the known findings are about vesting issues.

verdicts.title: Private-listing whitelist is open self-registration, so the seller cannot choose buyers

a.reden: The candidate describes a whitelist self‑registration issue, which is unrelated to the vesting‑related findings listed.

b.reden: The candidate finding concerns whitelist self-registration in SecondSwap_Whitelist, while known findings are about vesting calculations in the marketplace and vesting manager.

verdicts.title: Self-purchase of own listing inflates `bought` and bypasses maxSellPercent cap

a.reden: The candidate describes a self‑purchase bypass of the maxSellPercent cap, which is unrelated to the stepsClaimed inheritance or releaseRate miscalculations in the known findings.

b.reden: The candidate concerns self-purchase inflating `bought` to bypass the maxSellPercent cap, while the known findings concern incorrect `stepsClaimed`/`releaseRate` handling in `transferVesting`.

verdicts.title: transferVesting resets grantor releaseRate ignoring claimed steps, allowing over-claim from pooled tokens

a.reden: Both describe transferVesting resetting grantorVesting.releaseRate without accounting for already claimed amount, enabling over‑claim.

b.reden: The candidate describes the same incorrect releaseRate calculation in transferVesting that ignores claimed steps, leading to over-claim, which is the root cause of H-03.

verdicts.title: Existing holder receiving vesting gets retroactive early unlock of purchased tokens (incoming stepsClaimed ignored)

a.reden: Both describe misuse of stepsClaimed in transferVesting/_createVesting causing premature token unlock

b.reden: Both describe _createVesting ignoring the incoming stepsClaimed when adding to an existing vesting, causing retroactive unlock of newly transferred tokens in the VestingManager context.

verdicts.title: Step duration rounds down to zero or leaves currentStep above numOfSteps, causing DoS or underflow

a.reden: The candidate describes a stepDuration rounding/underflow issue, which is unrelated to the known findings about stepsClaimed inheritance or releaseRate miscalculation.

b.reden: The candidate describes a rounding issue in stepDuration calculation leading to DoS/underflow, which is not covered by any of the known findings.

verdicts.title: Discount percentage is not validated, so a listing can become unpurchasable

a.reden: The candidate describes a discount validation underflow bug, which is unrelated to the known findings about vesting stepsClaimed inheritance or releaseRate miscalculations.

b.reden: The candidate finding is about discount percentage validation in listVesting/_getDiscountedPrice, while known findings are about vesting transfer and stepsClaimed issues.

verdicts.title: Manager's pooled vesting carries first lister's stepsClaimed to all buyers and unlisters

a.reden: Both describe that the first listed vesting's stepsClaimed is inherited and affects later buyers' claim amounts

b.reden: The candidate describes the same root cause: the manager's vesting record inherits stepsClaimed from the first listing, affecting all subsequent buyers and unlisters.

verdicts.title: Whitelist for private listings is open self-registration, so access control is ineffective and can be griefed

a.reden: The candidate describes an access control issue in whitelist logic, unrelated to the vesting transfer bugs of H-01, H-02, or H-03.

b.reden: The candidate describes a whitelist access control flaw in SecondSwap_Whitelist.sol, while all known findings concern vesting calculation errors in the marketplace/vesting manager.

verdicts.title: setTokenOwner is irreversible and one-shot per owner, with broad token-owner power over vestings

a.reden: The candidate describes a different issue (irreversible setTokenOwner) not covered by H-01, H-02, or H-03.

b.reden: The candidate concerns irreversible setTokenOwner permissions and broad token-owner authority, not the transferVesting stepsClaimed or releaseRate calculation flaws in the known findings.

verdicts.title: Transfer into a fresh vesting from a grantor with all steps claimed reverts with division by zero

a.reden: The candidate describes a division‑by‑zero bug from releaseRate calculation with stepsClaimed equal to numOfSteps, which is not covered by any of the listed findings.

b.reden: The candidate describes a division-by-zero revert in _createVesting, while the known findings concern incorrect stepsClaimed/releaseRate causing premature token unlocking, not this DoS root cause.

verdicts.title: Default penaltyFee of 10 ether is applied to a 6-decimal USDT, making early unlisting impossible

a.reden: The candidate describes a penalty fee decimal mismatch, which is unrelated to the vesting stepsClaimed or releaseRate issues in the known findings.

b.reden: The candidate concerns an incorrectly scaled default penaltyFee blocking unlisting, while the known findings concern vesting stepsClaimed/releaseRate accounting bugs.

verdicts.title: Replacing the vesting manager desyncs existing StepVesting authorisations and strands listed tokens

a.reden: The candidate describes a manager address desynchronization, which is a different root cause than the stepsClaimed or releaseRate issues in the known findings.

b.reden: The candidate finding describes a desynchronization due to changing the vesting manager, which is not covered by any of the known findings (H-01, H-02, H-03).
